solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Drink a little king knocked over big cheeses (8)

indicators.note: something knocked over ends up the other way round

annotation.surface: A small king is felled by a drink, and the big cheeses look on.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A little king' looks like one idea, a minor monarch, but it splits into two pieces, SOME and R, which then turn round together.
annotation.definitionFit: Big cheeses is slang for the people in charge, and supremo is the informal word for a boss.

clue.text: Gift from France by tasteful tie or pants (6,2,7)

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are made a mess of

annotation.surface: A present from France: will it be a tasteful tie or some underwear?
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pants' reads as a noun in the list of gifts, but in British slang it is an adjective meaning rubbish, which makes it the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by history: France gave the New York monument to the United States in 1886.

clue.text: One stuck in rubbish opening of cat flap (5)

indicators.note: the one is stuck inside the other letters
the opening of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: to pan = to rubbish, criticise harshly

annotation.surface: Something is jammed in the cat flap, and it is rubbish.
annotation.walkthrough: I goes into PAN + C, between the N and the C. 'Cat flap' reads as one thing, but flap is split off as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to be in a flap is to be in a state of alarm.

clue.text: Old specialist having shaken blues is jubilant (8)

indicators.note: to shake something off is to get rid of it

blocks.note: a consultant is a senior hospital specialist
the Conservatives, whose colour is blue; removed from CONSULTANT

annotation.surface: A retired specialist has got over his depression and is delighted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blues' looks like low spirits; in British politics the blues are the Conservatives, CONS for short.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe triumphant delight.

clue.text: Blemish found on the bottom of old award (5)

indicators.note: in a down entry, the blemish sits below the O

annotation.surface: A mark on someone's backside, from long ago.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'on the bottom of' places SCAR beneath O; the surface wants bottom to mean someone's backside.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the nickname of the Academy's film statuette.

clue.text: Old country in a continent leader has fled (6)

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, and once it has fled, the word starts from its second letter

blocks.note: per = in a, as in miles per hour
Asia is a continent; losing its first letter leaves SIA

annotation.surface: A leader has fled from an old country somewhere in a continent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In a' looks like a link to the continent, but it is PER.
annotation.definitionFit: The historical name of Iran, used abroad until 1935, so an old country.

clue.text: Corroding European silver-plated container (6)

indicators.note: plating is a coat round the outside, so the silver wraps the container

blocks.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

annotation.surface: A silver-plated European pot is rusting away.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Silver-plated' reads as one adjective describing the pot; split it and the silver becomes a coat round the container.
annotation.definitionFit: Acid that is gradually wearing metal away is doing just what corroding describes.

clue.text: Son studying about power dissemination (9)

indicators.note: about = around, so S + READING goes round P

blocks.note: to read a subject at university is to study it

annotation.surface: A son is studying the topic of power distribution.
annotation.walkthrough: P goes just after the S of S + READING. 'Reading' for studying is the British university usage: you read law.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: dissemination is the act of scattering news or ideas widely.

clue.text: Snob messing with Irish urinal has a bad time (5,10)

indicators.note: to mess with something is to jumble it

annotation.surface: A snob who defaces an Irish toilet is having a rough time of it.
annotation.walkthrough: The Queen called 1992 her annus horribilis, a phrase that stuck in British speech.
annotation.definitionFit: Latin for horrible year, the phrase stands for any stretch of misfortune.

clue.text: Outrageous fence? (8)

blocks.note: used loosely: a shocking waste is a crime

annotation.surface: A garden fence so ugly it is an outrage.
annotation.walkthrough: The fence is not a garden barrier but a dealer in stolen goods; the question mark flags the second sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: loosely, shockingly bad, as in a waste of food; literally, a lawbreaker, which a receiver of stolen goods is.

clue.text: MC Hammer or nun with acne (9)

indicators.note: to hammer something is to batter it out of shape

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters; with just joins the parts

annotation.surface: A choice between the rapper MC Hammer and a spotty nun.
annotation.walkthrough: MC Hammer is a rapper, so the eye glues the two words together; split them and MC is the definition, Hammer the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A master of ceremonies introduces each act, so the job title is a synonym.

clue.text: Foreign city perhaps right to cordon off isle (5)

indicators.note: a cordon goes round the thing it closes off

blocks.note: your turn = your right to go next

annotation.surface: A city abroad perhaps has the right to seal off an island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' belongs to the definition: the answer is one example of a foreign city.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a city in northern Italy, foreign to a British setter.

clue.text: A French track overgrown with grass? (5)

blocks.note: a cut is a channel or track dug through ground

annotation.surface: A path in France that has grassed over.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark warns that the definition is by example: grass is only one thing that can be left unmown.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a lawn left unmown grows long and overgrown.

clue.text: Europeans travelling around San Marino (9)

indicators.note: letters that travel around end up in new places

annotation.surface: Some Europeans are touring the tiny state of San Marino.
annotation.walkthrough: San Marino is a tiny republic inside Italy, which makes the travelling Europeans look like tourists.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: people from a country in eastern Europe.

clue.text: I deliver vocals with music producer directing (10)

blocks.note: to sing is to deliver vocals

annotation.surface: A singer says they are doing the vocals while a record producer runs the session.
annotation.walkthrough: A music producer is usually a person in a studio; here it is an instrument.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: running an event means directing it.

clue.text: German rings essentially sell weed (9)

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, its middle letters

blocks.note: rings and rounds are both circles

annotation.surface: A German with rings is basically selling marijuana.
annotation.walkthrough: Weed looks like cannabis being sold in the surface; it is a garden plant.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a common yellow-flowered plant gardeners pull up.

clue.text: Get cracking piston fixed around ten, not noon (4,2,2)

indicators.note: a thing fixed is put right, rearranged
the rearranged PISTON goes round TE
'not' tells you the N, standing for noon, is to be left out of TEN

blocks.note: TEN without N, the noon abbreviation

annotation.surface: A mechanic fixes a piston at about ten, well before noon: get going!
annotation.walkthrough: 'Get cracking' looks like breaking something mechanical; it is the idiom for hurry. N is the usual short form of noon.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: pressing the accelerator pedal down means going faster, so hurrying.

clue.text: Reach with difficulty old chap who can’t get off Madeira? (4)

definitions.text: chap who can’t get off Madeira?

blocks.note: to win a summit is to reach it with effort

annotation.surface: An old man is stranded on the island of Madeira and struggles to get anywhere.
annotation.walkthrough: Madeira is an island, which makes 'can't get off' look like being stranded; it is also a fortified wine.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition: a heavy drinker who cannot get off the bottle, here a bottle of Madeira.

clue.text: Gas left by son in places where people get high? (8)

blocks.note: port = the left side of a ship

annotation.surface: A son left gas in places where people take drugs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Get high' suggests drugs, and gas fuels that reading; the question mark covers the flying sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition: planes take off from these places and passengers climb into the sky.

clue.text: Country girl shortly to win boy’s heart (4)

indicators.note: cut short, losing a last letter
the girl wins, takes in, the letter
the heart of a word is its middle letter

annotation.surface: A country girl hopes to win a boy's heart.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Country girl' reads as one phrase, but country is the definition. O goes between LA and S.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a landlocked nation in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Rebelling about Republican cuts, I start ding-dong (4,6)

definitions.note: the definition is the bell ringer speaking, so it names him in the first person

indicators.note: about = all around, in disorder
the Republican cuts into the other letters

annotation.surface: A rebellious American protests Republican spending cuts and starts a row.
annotation.walkthrough: Ding-dong is British for a noisy quarrel, which fits the political surface; here it is the sound of the bells.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition in the first person: the one who sets the church bells chiming.

clue.text: Work in which a beat is repeated from the start (2,4)

indicators.note: the next letters go in the work

annotation.surface: A piece of music in which the rhythm is played again from the beginning.
annotation.walkthrough: The musical surface makes 'beat' a rhythm; it is CAP, as in cap that story.
annotation.definitionFit: A musical direction in Italian, from the head, telling the player to go back to the beginning.

clue.text: British in numbers touring a northern city abroad (9)

indicators.note: B + GALORE tours round, surrounds, A N

annotation.surface: Crowds of British tourists visit a city in the north of a foreign country.
annotation.walkthrough: A N goes in just after the B of B + GALORE. 'Northern city' looks like a unit, but northern is only N.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a large city in southern India, now officially Bengaluru.

clue.text: Chuck out cap Catholic left for page (5)

indicators.note: C leaves and P takes its place

annotation.surface: Someone throws away a Catholic's hat, left out for a page boy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a direction or an abbreviation, L; here it means departed.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to throw someone out, as from a school.

clue.text: Dead fruit that’s first come across in backwoods (5)

indicators.note: the first letter you come across in the word

annotation.surface: A dead fruit found out in the backwoods.
annotation.walkthrough: Dead is an adverb here, as in dead centre, which is also plumb centre.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are informal adverbs for exactly: dead centre, plumb in the middle.

clue.text: Posh head ousted from vegetable association (5)

indicators.note: the first letter is thrown out

blocks.note: an onion is a vegetable; losing its head leaves NION

annotation.surface: A snob is thrown out of the vegetable growers' society.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Posh head' looks like a toff in charge; posh is U alone and head goes with ousted.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a body of workers or a group of states joined together.

clue.text: A tyrant making a comeback one dreaded? (5)

indicators.note: coming back means running the other way

blocks.note: a tsar was an absolute ruler

annotation.surface: A feared tyrant is returning to power.
annotation.walkthrough: Dreaded suggests feared, which suits the tyrant; the question mark points to dreadlocks, worn by Rastafarians.
annotation.definitionFit: A pun: a Rastafarian typically wears dreadlocks, so is dreaded in a hairstyle sense.

clue.text: One quietly infiltrating military objective (9)

indicators.note: to infiltrate is to get inside

annotation.surface: A spy slips quietly into the army to reach a military target.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Military objective' reads as a target, but objective is the definition, an adjective. P goes after the M of MARTIAL.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both mean judging without bias.

clue.text: Guy making first starter from yams and chicken (6)

indicators.note: the new letter is put first, in place of the old one
a starter is the first letter

blocks.note: first letter of yams; it replaces the F

annotation.surface: A man serves a starter of yams and then chicken.
annotation.walkthrough: The menu surface makes chicken a main course; it is the adjective for cowardly.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both are informal adjectives for cowardly.

clue.text: They’re our guests and joke with us ultimately (4,4)

indicators.note: ultimately = at the end, the last letter

blocks.note: a one, as in have you heard the one about

annotation.surface: Our guests are in on the joke with us in the end.
annotation.walkthrough: Read 'joke with' as a unit and the parts fall into answer order; 'the one about' is the everyday name for a told joke.
annotation.definitionFit: Modern idiom for the partners an invitee may bring along to a wedding or party.
